ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: At the top of the figure is an R–C≡N fragment, R is connected to carbon, and there is a triple bond between carbon and nitrogen; there are curved arrows around it but the question requires ignoring the arrows. At the bottom of the figure is an ester/carbonyl fragment containing zinc bromide: on the right is a carbonyl C=O, and the carbonyl carbon is also connected to an O–R2; the carbonyl carbon is connected at the lower left to the alpha carbon, and this alpha carbon is connected to R1 and to BrZn. No ordinary covalent bond connection is drawn between the upper and lower fragments. Reasoning: After ignoring the arrows, for the upper R–C≡N fragment write R as a wildcard, giving *C#N. For the lower part, starting from R2 as a wildcard and connected through oxygen, write *OC(=O), then connect to the alpha carbon; this alpha carbon is connected to the R1 wildcard and [Zn]Br, so it is written as C(*)[Zn]Br. The whole lower part is *OC(=O)C(*)[Zn]Br. Since no connecting bond is drawn between the upper nitrile fragment and the lower zinc ester fragment, separate them with a dot, giving *C#N.*OC(=O)C(*)[Zn]Br.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First describe the molecular graph shown, ignoring all arrows. Convert the upper R–C≡N fragment to '*C#N'. Then convert the lower fragment by starting from the R2 wildcard attached through oxygen, giving '*OC(=O)', then continue to the alpha carbon bonded to R1 and ZnBr, giving 'C(*)[Zn]Br'. Join these into the lower fragment '*OC(=O)C(*)[Zn]Br'. Since the nitrile and zinc ester fragments are not connected by a drawn bond, combine them with a dot to obtain '*C#N.*OC(=O)C(*)[Zn]Br'.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中上方是一个 R–C≡N 片段，R 与碳相连，碳与氮之间为三键；周围有弯曲箭头但题目要求忽略箭头。图中下方是一个含锌溴的酯/羰基片段：右侧为羰基 C=O，羰基碳还连接到一个 O–R2；羰基碳左下连接到 alpha 碳，该 alpha 碳连接 R1，并连接到 BrZn。上下两个片段之间没有画出普通共价键连接。推理：忽略箭头后，上方 R–C≡N 片段把 R 写作通配符，得到 *C#N。下方从 R2 作为通配符并经氧连接开始，写为 *OC(=O)，再接到 alpha 碳；该 alpha 碳连接 R1 通配符和 [Zn]Br，因此写作 C(*)[Zn]Br。下方整体为 *OC(=O)C(*)[Zn]Br。由于上方腈片段和下方锌酯片段没有画出连接键，用点号分隔，得到 *C#N.*OC(=O)C(*)[Zn]Br。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the single natural route: parse the drawn chemical connectivity while explicitly disregarding the curved arrows, then translate each disconnected fragment into SMILES with wildcards for R, R1, and R2.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the image as two disconnected structural fragments. The upper fragment is R–C≡N, with the R group attached to the nitrile carbon. The lower fragment is an ester/enolate-like zinc bromide complex: Br–Zn bonded to the alpha carbon; that alpha carbon is also bonded to R1 and to a carbonyl carbon; the carbonyl carbon is double-bonded to O and single-bonded to OR2. Ignore the curved arrows entirely.
planner_metadata.text_role: Read the prompt instruction that asks for the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure and specifically says to ignore the arrows.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard SMILES syntax: represent generic R substituents as wildcard atoms '*'; use '#' for the C≡N triple bond; use '(=O)' for a carbonyl; use dot notation for disconnected fragments; bracket zinc as [Zn] and attach Br as [Zn]Br.
